prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends — I can find the highest-rated, properly certified Miami contractors near you if you give your ZIP code. Rather than name a single “best” company (which depends on your location, roof type, budget and insurance situation), here’s how to identify the best roofing contractor in Miami for a hurricane‑rated roof replacement and what to ask for.

What a top hurricane-rated roofer in Miami will have
- Miami‑Dade County approvals/NoA: installers who use materials with Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or comparable product approvals.  
- Florida Contractor license (check at Florida DBPR) and local business license.  
- General liability and workers’ comp insurance (verify certificates).  
- Manufacturer certification (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, Duro-Last, etc.) and ability to offer a manufacturer’s warranty.  
- Experience with code-required hurricane attachments: ring‑shank nails or screws, hurricane clips/straps, secondary water barrier, deck attachment methods that meet Florida Building Code.  
- Permitting and inspection experience (will pull permits and pass county inspections).  
- References and local portfolio of completed hurricane‑rated installations.  
- Good reviews (Google, Yelp) and an A-/A+ BBB rating if available.

Key questions to ask any prospective roofer
- Do you have a Florida State Roofing Contractor license and can you provide the number?  
- Are you licensed to work in Miami‑Dade County and do you carry workers’ comp and general liability? Ask for COI.  
- Which products do you recommend that have Miami‑Dade NOA? Can you provide the NOA numbers?  
- Are you factory‑certified with the shingle/manufacturer, and what warranties will I get (manufacturer and workmanship)?  
- How will you secure my roof to meet the Florida Building Code (nailing pattern, deck attachment, straps/clips, secondary barrier)?  
- Who will pull the permits and handle inspections?  
- Can you provide 3 local references for hurricane‑rated roof replacements completed in the last 2 years?  
- How will you protect landscaping and handle cleanup? What is the payment schedule?

Red flags
- No permit or “permit optional” responses.  
- No proof of insurance or license.  
- Pressure to pay large sums in cash or “special” discounts for immediate payment.  
- Vague answers about product approvals (NOA) or installation details.  
- Very low estimate that’s far below other bids.

Other practical steps
- Get at least 3 written estimates with itemized scopes (tear-off vs. recover, underlayment type, flashing, fasteners, edge metal, warranty).  
- Verify license/insurance on Florida DBPR and ask to see the Miami‑Dade job card or permit record after the permit is pulled.  
- Check manufacturer warranty fine print (what voids it, what is covered, transferability).  
- Use a written contract with start/end dates, payment schedule, scope and cleanup clause.  
- Coordinate with your insurance company if replacement is due to storm damage — reputable roofers will help with documentation.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated Miami roofers that meet these criteria in your ZIP code and show license/NOA/BBB status, or  
- Review 2–3 estimates and contracts and point out issues to watch for.

Tell me your ZIP code or paste the estimates/contracts and I’ll help find or evaluate contractors.
